attrInputHeight.name: input_height
attrInputHeight.label: input height
attrInputHeight.comment: The height of the surface above the geometry: bind the map which computes it. The map is evaluated three times, at the shading point and at two points next to it, and the normal is tilted by the slope between them

attrStrength.name: strength
attrStrength.comment: How much of the bumped normal is used: 0 leaves the normal as it is, 1 is the bumped normal. Negative values count as 0

attrDistance.name: distance
attrDistance.comment: The length a height of 1 stands for, in the units of the space the bump is computed in (see object_space)

attrInvert.name: invert
attrInvert.comment: Heights go into the surface instead of out of it

attrObjectSpace.name: object_space
attrObjectSpace.label: object space
attrObjectSpace.comment: Heights are lengths in the space of the object, so that the bumps scale with it; otherwise in world space

attrFilterWidth.name: filter_width
attrFilterWidth.label: filter width
attrFilterWidth.comment: How far apart the three evaluations of the height are, in pixels

attrInputNormal.name: input_normal
attrInputNormal.label: input normal
attrInputNormal.comment: The normal to bump instead of the shading normal, e.g. another bump or a normal map
